problem: Weights passed as a generator or iterator are consumed by the discarded _ref.allocate validation call, so line 19 sees no weights and the function silently returns [] and allocates none of the amount.

int(round(float(amount) * 10 ** places)) loses precision for large or high-precision amounts, so the shares no longer sum to the input amount (e.g. "90071992547409.93" over [1] returns one cent more).
Converting validated Decimal weights to float turns tiny weights into 0.0 (ZeroDivisionError) and huge weights into inf (NaN ValueError), so inputs the validation accepts crash.

Sorting on float remainders sends the leftover units to the wrong recipients and breaks the lowest-index tie-break rule even for small amounts (e.g. "0.02" over ["3","15","4"] gives [0.00, 0.01, 0.01] instead of [0.00, 0.02, 0.00]).
Truncating float shares with int() can make leftover negative, and order[:leftover] then adds a unit to most shares, so the function pays out more than the amount.

Production code imports reference_impl and runs its full allocation only for validation, discarding both the result and the converted values, which doubles the work and ties this module's input rules to another file.
